records.title: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) Plant Extracts Affect the Cytochrome P450 System and Cytotoxicity of Primary Human Hepatocytes
records.source_title: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) Plant Extracts Affect the Cytochrome P450 System and Cytotoxicity of Primary Human Hepatocytes
records.abstract: Primary human hepatocyte cultures were exposed to root and leaf ashwagandha extracts prepared with water or ethanol. An ethanol root extract altered CYP3A4 expression and activity, and a high-concentration ethanol leaf extract affected cell viability across time and concentration. These are laboratory observations rather than clinical interaction findings.
records.relevance_reason: Primary botanical pharmacology evidence requiring study-design-aware scientific review.
records.study_design: Primary human hepatocyte CYP expression and viability assays
records.intervention: Botanical extract and purified constituent experimental comparison
records.comparator: Extracts, constituent fractions, or assay controls
outcomes: Ethanol root extract modulated CYP3A4 expression and activity
High-concentration ethanol leaf extract reduced viability with time and concentration
records.uncertainty: Laboratory results are not evidence of clinical effectiveness or clinically meaningful interaction.
records.adverse_effects: No clinical adverse events measured; laboratory outcomes only.
records.interactions: Preclinical mechanistic effects only; no human drug-interaction trial.
records.limitations: In vitro models and extract-dependent chemistry limit translation to humans.
